why: The answer depends on the date the Government of India introduced Joint Forest Management - the 1980s - as its way of working with local communities to protect and manage forests.
note: Topic gap. The Environmental Issues list carries four pollution rows and no 'Unspecified Topic' placeholder, so the whole deforestation half of the chapter - jhum cultivation, reforestation, the Chipko movement, Amrita Devi Bishnoi, JFM (verified at ncert BIO12O ch16 p015-p016) - has no home. Filing JFM under a pollution row would be plainly wrong; Biodiversity and Conservation's 'How Do We Conserve Biodiversity' row was the tempting cross-chapter dodge, but reaching into another chapter is not allowed and the chapter choice was verified against the NCERT page.
proposed_topic: Deforestation and People's Participation in Forest Conservation (Chipko Movement, Joint Forest Management)
